title: Secretin: the first hormone
detail: William Bayliss and Ernest Starling showed that a substance from the gut lining, which they named secretin, stimulates the pancreas through the blood. It was the first hormone ever identified, and it is a peptide.

title: Solid-phase peptide synthesis
detail: Bruce Merrifield anchored a growing peptide chain to resin beads, turning slow solution chemistry into a repeatable, automatable cycle. Almost every synthetic peptide in this atlas is made this way.

title: Nobel Prize for peptide hormones of the brain
detail: Roger Guillemin and Andrew Schally shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering hypothalamic peptide hormones such as TRH, GnRH and somatostatin, with Rosalyn Yalow for radioimmunoassays of peptide hormones.

title: Nobel Prize for Merrifield
detail: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised solid-phase synthesis, the method behind today's industrial peptide manufacturing.

title: AlphaFold 2 solves structure prediction
detail: DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 predicted protein structures with near-experimental accuracy at the CASP14 assessment, opening the way to predicted models for sequences never crystallised.

title: ESMFold and the ESM Metagenomic Atlas
detail: Meta AI released ESMFold, a language-model-based structure predictor fast enough to fold hundreds of millions of sequences. The predicted models in this atlas come from ESMFold.

title: Nobel Prize for protein design and structure prediction
detail: David Baker, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design and AlphaFold.
